questions.q: Where do native Salesforce reports and dashboards get their data?
questions.explain: Native reports query Salesforce records live. CRM Analytics and Tableau Next work from other data layers.

questions.q: Which layer sits between Data 360 objects and Tableau Next visualizations?
questions.explain: The semantic model defines objects, relationships, and measures once, so every visualization inherits the same definitions.

questions.q: A CRM Analytics number and a native report number disagree. Which is a plausible reason based on the layers in this lesson?
options: Native reports never include closed records
The CRM Analytics dataset was last refreshed before recent record changes, while the report queries live records
Tableau Next is secretly modifying both
Dashboards always round numbers to the nearest thousand
questions.explain: Refresh timing is the classic cause: datasets are loaded on a schedule, while native reports read live data.

questions.q: What is Salesforce's stated position on the relationship between Tableau Next and CRM Analytics, per this lesson?
options: CRM Analytics was deleted from the platform
Tableau Next is the pathway to the newest AI capabilities, and CRM Analytics continues for customers not ready to move
Tableau Next only works for marketing teams
questions.explain: Salesforce describes Tableau Next as the pathway to newer generative AI and agentic capabilities while CRM Analytics continues. Verify roadmap claims against current release notes.

questions.q: In the Data 360 layer, what does harmonizing mean?
options: Mapping data from different sources into standardized data model objects
Playing audio in the Analytics Studio
questions.explain: Harmonizing maps ingested data into standard structures so different sources can be treated consistently.
